title: Market Metro — Agentic Commerce That Learns

style.captions: Two lines maximum; keep disclosures readable
style.motion: Slow push-ins, brief highlights and clean cuts; do not fabricate UI actions

production.capture: Real app interaction clips using saved data; Remotion edits the captured footage
production.audio: Record the approved voiceover or use an agreed local voice; no paid TTS call yet

scenes.title: Start inside the economy
scenes.captureAction: Keep Day 1 visible. Pan across stores, shoppers and the PayPal building. Use real recorded app footage.
scenes.narration: This is Market Metro: twelve merchants and six hundred simulated shoppers. They browse, buy, and receive deliveries. Their activity becomes the data our AI planner uses to investigate demand, train models, and test campaigns.

scenes.title: Make the business decision concrete
scenes.captureAction: Advance to Agent decisions, first stop. Highlight electronics and furniture interest versus funded units.
scenes.narration: The business question: who should we contact, and what should we recommend? Interest alone does not guarantee a funded purchase, or an order the merchant can fulfill.

scenes.title: Show the data contract
scenes.captureAction: In the feed verifier, show a split checkout, then the ambiguous-link hold. Label this as a separate data-quality demonstration.
scenes.narration: Our ontology verifier counts split checkouts once and holds ambiguous relationships. In a separate twenty-four-feed test, it accepted all twelve usable merchant exports, versus six for fixed mapping. Both methods held all twelve unsafe exports.

scenes.title: Show the LLM choosing work
scenes.captureAction: Open the same campaign in AG Studio. In Agent decisions, inspect Day 31 Analyze and Train; then show Model training with two distinct model bars and its native AG Grid registry. Keep the AG Studio/AG Grid caption visible.
scenes.narration: Back in our recorded campaign, the LLM investigates demand, chooses a twenty-eight-day market-feedback window, and requests two local model fits. It proposes ranked recommendations and shopping-needs inquiries for up to thirty-six consenting shoppers a day. These are saved decisions from a real model run, with the inputs and tool results available to inspect.
onScreen: AG Studio · model registry and recorded decisions

scenes.title: Show why the model changed
scenes.captureAction: Choose Agent decisions, then Next to the model-change stop. Highlight the two development-trial rows and selected boosted model.
scenes.narration: The LLM preferred a two-stage response model. The verifier tested both rankings with the same campaign in three development markets. Boosted trees earned more and passed the merchant and purchase checks, so the verifier selected it. The LLM proposes; trusted tools govern execution.
onScreen: Selected before measuring this market’s later outcomes

scenes.title: Follow one shopper
scenes.captureAction: Advance to Shopper response. Focus Form & Function and the Day 35 purchase → Day 36 delivery trace.
scenes.narration: Shopper one-seventy-nine had not bought for sixteen days. After a recommendation, they buy a ninety-six-dollar mobile side table and receive it the next day. Under fixed rules, the same request went unfilled.

scenes.title: Connect the purchase to PayPal
scenes.captureAction: Show this campaign’s native receipt, its capture ID, fee and test merchant proceeds. Briefly open the warehouse-order link.
scenes.narration: That exact warehouse order was mirrored once through PayPal Sandbox. Here is the completed ninety-six-dollar capture: a three-dollar-fifty-six fee and ninety-two dollars forty-four in test merchant proceeds. PayPal supplies the execution and receipt proof. The simulated payment economics let us compare campaigns without charging real shoppers.
onScreen: One existing sale; never counted twice

scenes.title: Show the matched gain
scenes.captureAction: Use AG Studio Net profits for this same campaign. Show native AG Charts fixed-versus-planner bars and the AG Grid settled-comparison rows, then emphasize the three gains. Preserve the simulation and inventory labels.
scenes.narration: After settlement, the campaign produced sixteen more retained purchases, over a thousand dollars in additional merchant contribution, and three point four seven percent higher modeled PayPal net than fixed rules. Estimated model usage was roughly three cents. These are simulated results, not production profit.
onScreen: One paired simulation · contribution includes inventory

scenes.title: Show AG Grid as the evidence workspace
scenes.captureAction: Sort the model registry by Recommendation AUROC, filter the decision ledger with the Day 31 Verify stage, show the custom PayPal widget, then enable Arrange and resize one dashboard widget. Use actual app interactions from the same saved campaign.
scenes.narration: AG Grid and AG Charts, inside AG Studio, make the workflow inspectable. Sort the model registry, follow a decision back to its evidence, and reconcile payments in our custom PayPal widget. The same dashboards compare fixed rules with the published campaign, and their layouts can be rearranged.
onScreen: AG Studio · AG Grid · AG Charts
Inspect models → explain decisions → reconcile payments
Custom PayPal widget · editable dashboard layout

captureSteps.action: Click the Recommendation AUROC column header to sort the training registry. Keep both model names and actual scores visible.
Choose Day 31 Verify. Show the filtered AG Grid checkpoint rows and open the recorded verifier evidence.
Show the custom PayPal evidence widget: one native capture, alongside the receipt reconciliation grid.
Enable Arrange and resize one widget. Do not imply that the LLM generated the layout or that the edit persists.

scenes.title: Close on the product
scenes.captureAction: End on the Market → Agent decisions → Impact navigation with the project title. Keep the free saved-policy exploration link readable.
scenes.narration: Market Metro. Agentic commerce that learns, and shows its work.

uploadDraft.description:
Market Metro turns observed merchant activity into trained models, tested campaigns and traceable PayPal payments. This demo follows one saved 12-store, 600-shopper simulation from Day 1 to a recorded agent decision, purchase and native PayPal Sandbox receipt.

Against fixed rules in that same simulation: 16 more retained purchases, $1,024.86 additional merchant contribution, and $114.96 higher modeled PayPal net after estimated model cost. Merchant contribution includes inventory value. These are simulated outcomes, not actual PayPal profit. The $96 Sandbox capture is an existing order and uses fictitious funds.

Built with PayPal Sandbox, Gemini on Vertex AI, local scikit-learn models, SQLite, Three.js and AG Studio with native AG Grid, AG Charts and a custom PayPal evidence widget. The ontology feed comparison is a separate synthetic-data test.

Source and setup: https://github.com/VinceVence/market-metro
Original code: MIT. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
